column3: NKJV reads לַפִּיד (“to disaster”) as “a lamp,” giving “A lamp is despised,” a different division of the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; the last line is rendered interpretively, “In what God provides by His hand.”
Close to the Hebrew; שׁוֹלָל (“barefoot, stripped”) is rendered “plundered.”
Close to the Hebrew; מוּסַר (“discipline, bond”) is rendered “the bonds,” and “loincloth” “belt.”
Close to the Hebrew; כֹּהֲנִים (“priests”) is rendered “princes,” and “barefoot” “plundered.”
Close to the Hebrew; “loosens the belt of the strong” is rendered “disarms the mighty.”
Close to the Hebrew; צַלְמָוֶת (“deep darkness”) is rendered “the shadow of death.”
Close to the Hebrew; לֵב (“heart”) is rendered “understanding.”
